text:
Priyanka Rao: Heads up — I moved from NJ to NYC midpay period (moved 2025-09-14). My Sep paycheck shows NJ state withholding + a NYC local line item. I updated address in Workday on 9/15 but pay was processed 9/16. Can someone confirm how the splitter works and whether this will be fixed on W-2? Also my PTO cashout was prorated and marked as NJ earnings in the system.
Alex Chen: Thanks for flagging — can you share your Redwood employee ID (not SSN) and the pay period dates?
Priyanka Rao: emp-04572. Pay period was 9/1-9/15 and 9/16-9/30 (semi-monthly). I moved midday on the 14th so most days in the first half were NJ, second half NYC.
Samir Patel: Got it — quick note: payroll calculates state withholding based on the employee address on file at the payroll cutoff for that payrun. Municipal/local taxes depend on the work location flag and employer location. If you changed your address after cutoff, that explains NJ withholding.
Samir Patel: We'll need to split income across states by days in period and re-run a retro adjustment for the 9/16 payrun if appropriate. For the PTO cashout tagged to NJ, we can reclass that too. Please attach a copy of your NYC lease or utility bill to the payroll ticket so we have proof of move date.
Priyanka Rao: Ok attaching lease now (uploaded to the ticket). What does retro adjustment look like and timeline?
Samir Patel: We'll create a retro payroll correction that posts reversing entries in the next payrun and issues any net pay difference as an off-cycle or on the next scheduled regular run (depends on the amount). If withholding was under/over-withheld, we'll adjust state withholding and any local tax removal/add. If W-2 needs a change after year-end, we can issue a W-2c. Expect 1-2 pay cycles for processing.
Payroll Bot: Ticket #HR-2025-1123 created and assigned to payroll for investigation. Attachments: pri-lease.pdf
Maya Li: For future moves — if you update your address and residency info before the payroll cutoff (usually 2 business days prior to run), the system will pick up the new state for that payrun. If a move is mid-period we typically split by days unless the employee elects resident treatment earlier and provides proof.
Alex Chen: FYI — could impact benefits deductions if residency changes (state tax credits / pre-tax benefits). Priyanka, we'll confirm after payroll completes the split.
Priyanka Rao: Thanks everyone — appreciate the fast response. Will monitor ticket and let you know if anything else pops up. :white_check_mark:
